chapters.title: 1. Intro to Color Theory
chapters.content:
Color is one of the most powerful tools in a designer's toolkit. It can draw attention, set a mood, influence users' emotions, perceptions, and actions.

Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary Colors

Pro Tip: 60-30-10 Rule
Use the 60-30-10 rule for color schemes: 60% dominant color, 30% secondary color, and 10% accent color.

chapters.title: 2. Typography Basics
chapters.content:
Typography is the art and technique of arranging type to make written language legible, readable, and appealing when displayed.

Font Families

Always pair a legible sans-serif font for UI elements with a complementary serif or sans-serif for long-form reading content. Limit your interface to no more than 2-3 different font families to maintain consistency.

Hierarchy

Establish visual hierarchy by manipulating size, weight, and color. A page title should be instantly recognizable compared to paragraph text.

chapters.title: 3. Spacing & Grid Systems
chapters.content:
Whitespace (or negative space) is the empty space between and around elements of a design or page layout. It is often neglected but it is what gives a layout breathing room.

The 8pt Grid System

Many modern interfaces use an 8-point grid system. This means that margins, padding, and sometimes even element dimensions are multiples of 8 (8, 16, 24, 32, 40, etc.). This creates a rhythmic, predictable visual flow.

chapters.title: 4. Web Accessibility (a11y)
chapters.content:
Accessibility means designing and developing websites so that people with disabilities can use them.

Contrast Ratio

Ensure your text color contrasts adequately with its background. WCAG requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for standard text.

Alt Text & ARIA

Always provide alt text for images. Use ARIA (Accessible Rich Internet Applications) attributes to define the roles and states of custom UI components for screen readers.

Empathy in Design
Designing for accessibility often results in a better user experience for everyone, not just those with permanent disabilities.
